name: Bulungan
confidence_why: Adul, Ismail and Effendi 1985 and Beech 1908 (with Fokker's appendix) both put main stress on the penult and both treat it as non-contrastive, differing only in details, namely Fokker's exception that a schwa penult throws the accent onto the final syllable and whether the enclitic na moves the accent; the other works consulted (Adul et al. 1990, Lobel 2013, Aritonang et al. 2002) say nothing abo…

catalog_quote: Fonem suprasegmental tidak terdapat dalam bahasa Bulungan. Perbedaan tekanan, nada, dan kualitas (panjang-pendek) tidak membedakan arti kata. Morfem, seperti partikel /na/, yang dapat diterjemahkan dengan partikel "lah" dalam bahasa Indonesia, dalam pemakaiannya hanya menjadi ciri pemberian tekanan dalam pengucapan pada kata sebelumnya, misalnya /kilána/ 'tidaklah', /bagína/ 'janganlah', dan /betitona/ 'sekaranglah'. Secara fonetis, tekanan kata dalam bahasa Bulungan mempunyai pola tekanan utama pada suku kedua dari belakang. Perubahan hanya terjadi dalam situasi tertentu. Contoh: méndus 'mandi', túmbung 'pantat', píntor 'pintar', kíla 'tidak', bági 'jangan'; mendúsna 'mandilah', taméqni 'paman', tetúmbu 'bakul besar', kilána 'tidaklah', bagína 'janganlah'.

new_statements.quote: Fonem suprasegmental tidak terdapat dalam bahasa Bulungan. Perbedaan tekanan, nada, dan kualitas (panjang-pendek) tidak membedakan arti kata. Morfem, seperti partikel /na/, yang dapat diterjemahkan dengan partikel "lah" dalam bahasa Indonesia, dalam pemakaiannya hanya menjadi ciri pemberian tekanan dalam pengucapan pada kata sebelumnya, misalnya /kilána/ 'tidaklah', /bagína/ 'janganlah', dan /betitona/ 'sekaranglah'. Secara fonetis, tekanan kata dalam bahasa Bulungan mempunyai pola tekanan utama pada suku kedua dari belakang. Perubahan hanya terjadi dalam situasi tertentu. Contoh: méndus 'mandi', túmbung 'pantat', píntor 'pintar', kíla 'tidak', bági 'jangan'; mendúsna 'mandilah', taméqni 'paman', tetúmbu 'bakul besar', kilána 'tidaklah', bagína 'janganlah'.
new_statements.translation: There are no suprasegmental phonemes in Bulungan. Differences of stress, pitch and quantity (long-short) do not distinguish word meanings. A morpheme such as the particle /na/, which can be translated with Indonesian 'lah', in use merely marks emphasis in the pronunciation of the preceding word, e.g. /kilána/ 'tidaklah', /bagína/ 'janganlah', /betitona/ 'sekaranglah'. Phonetically, word stress in Bulungan has the pattern of main stress on the second syllable from the end. Change occurs only in certain situations. Examples: méndus 'bathe', túmbung 'buttocks', píntor 'clever', kíla 'not', bági 'don't'; mendúsna 'do bathe', taméqni 'uncle', tetúmbu 'large basket', kilána 'not (emph.)', bagína 'don't (emph.)'.
new_statements.citation: Adul, M. Asfandi; Abdurachman Ismail; Rustam Effendi. 1985. Struktur Bahasa Bulungan. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan.

The embedded scanned layer ( lines 1363-1380) matches apart from s…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive and falls on the penultimate syllable of the word; when the emphatic enclitic /na/ is attached, stress moves to the new penult (kíla > kilána), i.e. the domain includes the enclitic. Beech 1908 (p. 19) independently gives penultimate accent for Bolongan, and Fokker's appendix (p. 109) adds that a schwa penult throws the accent onto the final syllable (Bol. tĕrắng, kĕpá', gĕnáp); Adul et al. do not state a schwa exception and mark méndus with penult stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source opened.
new_statements.exceptions: Adul et al.: 'Perubahan hanya terjadi dalam situasi tertentu' (changes only in certain situations), illustrated only by the enclitic-/na/ shift. Fokker in Beech 1908 p. 109: penult containing ĕ (schwa) is skipped, accent then final; p. 109 sec. 8: suffix-induced shift to new penult only for vowel-final words (pupús-nia keeps original accent).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, citation forms with acute marks; enclitic /na/ counts for stress placement (phonological word = host + enclitic). Fieldwork Tanjung Palas / Tanjung Selor, Kab. Bulungan, 1981/82.
new_statements.identity_note: Adul et al. 1985 describe 'bahasa Bulungan' of the former Bulungan sultanate, informants from Tanjung Palas and Tanjung Selor (Kab. Bulungan) = Glottolog bolo1268 Bolongan [blj] (Glottolog files this book under bolo1268). Beech 1908's 'Bolongan dialect of Tidong' is the same Bulungan language; Lobel 2013:401 notes it is not actually a Tidung variety (Glottolog: Sabahan, not Murutic/Tidong tido1248). Beech's general p. 19 rule covers Tarakan Tidong and Bolongan jointly; Fokker's p. 109 examples labelled 'Bolongan' are specific to this language.

new_statements.quote: p. 19: "For the pronunciation of words a general rule can be made that the accent falls on the penultimate, as in Malay, Dayak, Javanese, Sundanese, &c." — Appendix p. 109: "§ 7. Accent.—The general rule is: the accent lies on the penult, provided this does not contain ĕ (medio-palatal, French 'e muet'):— kápa', hatchet. dinándu, woman. nusáĭ, what? kasábay, arrived. Bolongan { tĕráŋ (voc. t'ràng), clear. kĕpá', curtailed. gĕnáp (voc. g'nap), enough, complete." ... "§ 8. ... Suffixes may cause a shift of accent to the new penult, the suffix being felt as part of the word to which it has been added, but only if the word ends in a vowel" ... "in pupus-nia, afterwards, the original accent remains"

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog rule (penult: penultimate stress) and as Adul et al. 1985 (main stress on the penult). Adds: schwa-penult exception (accent on the final: tĕráŋ, kĕpá', gĕnáp, given explicitly as Bolongan forms), accent shift to the new penult under suffixes only for vowel-final bases, causative pa- excluded from the count, and the claim that enclitic na does not move the accent. That last point differs from Adul et al. 1985, whose examples mendu'sna, kila'na, bagi'na show the stress moving to the new penult before /na/; see conflicts.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent falls on the penultimate syllable (Beech, stated for both Tidong dialects, Bolongan and Tarakan). Fokker's appendix refines: penult accent unless the penult vowel is schwa (e-muet), in which case the accent falls on the final syllable; his three Bolongan examples (tĕráŋ 'clear', kĕpá' 'curtailed', gĕnáp 'enough') all show this final-accent case. Suffixes count as part of the word and shift the accent to the new penult, but only when the base ends in a vowel (naŋkúbi from táŋkup; sāmá-mu); the particles nia (Tar.) / na (Bol.) 'already' are enclitic particles, not suffixes, and leave the original accent in place (pupus-nia). A vocabulary footnote (p. 58) notes that in pa-bāsi the causative prefix pa- is skipped and the accent falls on the second syllable, i.e. the stem's penult.
new_statements.exceptions: Schwa (ĕ) in the penult pushes the accent to the final syllable (Fokker sec. 7; all Bolongan examples given are of this type: tĕráŋ, kĕpá', gĕnáp). Accent shifts to the new penult under suffixation only when the base ends in a vowel; consonant-final bases keep their accent (sec. 8). Enclitic na/nia does not shift the accent (sec. 8 N.B.). Fokker adds that the schwa-penult case is extremely rare in Tarakan (mĕñjul), implying it is more common in Bolongan.
new_statements.identity_note: Beech 1908 treats 'Bolongan' as one of two dialects of Tidong (the other being Tarakan), with texts and vocabulary in both. Glottolog files it under bolo1268 Bulungan; Lobel 2013 (p. 401, already held by the project) classifies Bulungan as not closely related to Tidung, so Beech's 'Bolongan dialect' material is the Bulungan language proper, collected c. 1900s. The p. 19 penult statement is made for 'the Tidong dialects' generally (both Bolongan and Tarakan); in Fokker's Appendix sec. 7 the unlabelled examples are Tarakan and three examples are explicitly labelled Bolongan, all showing the schwa-penult/final-accent case.

readall_conflicts: Placement agrees across all sources (penult). Two details disagree. (1) Adul et al. 1985 (Struktur Bahasa Bulungan, sec. 3.7, p. 31) give mendu'sna, kila'na, bagi'na, i.e. stress moves to the new penult before the particle /na/; Fokker (Beech 1908, Appendix sec. 8, p. 109) says na (Bol.) / nia (Tar.) are enclitic particles, not suffixes, and that in pupus-nia 'the original accent remains' — though his one example is Tarakan and consonant-final, and his own rule that suffixes shift the accent only after vowel-final bases would in any case predict no shift for pupus; the Adul examples are vowel-final (kila, bagi) or consonant-final (mendus), so the two sources cannot be fully reconciled on the enclitic. (2) Fokker's schwa-penult exception (accent on the final in tĕráŋ, kĕpá', gĕnáp) is not mentioned by Adul et al. 1985, who state the penult rule without exceptions; neither is a direct contradiction of the catalog's penult rule, but the schwa exception is a refinement the catalog does not yet record. Adul et al. 1985 also state that stress is not phonemic ('Fonem suprasegmental tidak terdapat'), which Beech/Fokker do not address either way.
